:::{#sol-matrix-size-practice}

$\matr{C}$ has three [row](#def-matrix-row)s,
$\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$
and
$\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$,
and each row has two entries,
so $\matr{C}$ has two [column](#def-matrix-column)s.
So $m = 3$ and $n = 2$:
$\matr{C}$ is a $3 \times 2$ [matrix](#def-matrix),
with $3 \cd 2 = 6$ entries.

:::
